features: Client TUI Render Cleanup: Updated all section headers and divider lines to erase to end-of-line (\033[K), eliminating trailing character artifacts.
Inspector Replay Sanitization: Sanitized HTTP method strings during request replay, fixing net/http invalid method errors when replaying previously replayed requests.

Dynamic Region Auto-Failover on Node Shutdown: Set Chisel retry limits and added an outer failover loop so the client CLI automatically auto-detects edge node shutdowns and fails over to the next fastest online region.
Edge Health Monitoring Fix: Edge node health determination now reads directly from active WebSocket control channels and real-time remote IPs, eliminating false-positive 5ms loopback latency.
Windows CI Test Suite Fix: Fixed path backslash translation in Makefile test targets for cross-platform Git Bash compatibility across CI matrix runners.
Target Node Power Control: Added graceful AWS credential checks to Target Node Cost & Power Control scheduled workflow.
Dynamic Region Failover: When a requested or cached region is offline (e.g. apac), the client CLI automatically probes active regions and connects to the fastest online node.
Instant Edge Stop Sync: Stopping an edge node in Portal V2 immediately tears down active developer tunnels, closes the control channel, and marks node health as Offline.
Client TUI Active Region Display: The terminal header now displays the active region code and edge node hostname (e.g. apac (aws-edge-apac.lfr-demo.se)).
Gateway Edge Domain Routing: Central server gateway now correctly recognizes edge node domains as control plane endpoints.

What's New & Help bar: The old always-visible sidebar (What's New panel + Help & Resources card) is now a single collapsible bar at the top of the dashboard, minimized by default and auto-expanding once when there's something new to see.
Fixed the What's New & Help toggle being unclear -- it's now a proper outlined button with explicit Show/Hide text instead of a bare chevron.
Fixed What's New and Help & Resources not actually sitting side by side on wider screens once expanded.
